The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Board
of Trustees with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 4th Monday of every month at 8:00 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the  Community  Services Department via email  at
kshigenaga@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-0791 prior to the meeting for
assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Library Board of Trustees may teleconference into the meeting without
noticing each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public
meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
To protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, it is recommended that
members of the public wear a mask indoors, per the State and County Health
Department’s current Health Officer Orders. Given the seriousness of COVID-19, you
are encouraged to provide input electronically if you do not feel comfortable attending in
person.

SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND LIBRARY MANAGER REPORT

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Community Services Director and Library
Manager provide a monthly report to the Crowell Public Library Board of Trustees. The report
provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial updates, as well as information on
upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Update
Library Supervisors are currently recruiting for part-time (PT) Library Assistants. The goal is to
make offers by Mid-October. These positions provide reference, programming, and collection
development support to Adult Services and Youth Services. Staff also plan to fill vacant PT
customer service positions in Circulation. These positions assist with checking materials in and out
of the Library, provide patrons with account support, shelve materials, and provide passport
services.

Library A/C Status Update
During the recent heat wave, the Library experienced intermittent operating hours. This was
because one of two compressors for the heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system
chiller unit stopped functioning. Parks and Public Works staff and a HVAC contractor were able to
stabilize the system to operate at half capacity, using a secondary compressor. This allowed the
Library to remain cool enough to open from 10 AM to 2 PM; the Library was unable to remain
operable once the temperatures outside reached over 90 degrees. This was just a temporary fix;
what is needed is a new compressor. The City Council recently approved an emergency
procurement of $70K for the replacement equipment.

Emergency Cooling Center Operations
Community Services Department (CSD) staff recently oversaw the coordination and management
of the emergency Cooling Center at the San Marino Center for 10 days during the heat wave.

  Page 9 of 27
 Originally planned to be in the Barth Community Room, staff were quickly forced to relocate the
Cooling Center to the San Marino Center due to the A/C issue at the Library. During the 10-day
period, 413 individuals were served. Library and Recreation Division staff worked collaboratively
to man the Center from 10 AM to 7 PM daily. Patrons were also provided bottled water and free
access to Wi-Fi.

Recreation Commission Comes Off of Hiatus
A new 5-member City Council-appointed Recreation Commission held its first meeting on
September 12. Some may recall that this citizen advisory body was placed on hiatus back in March
2020 while the City Administration and Council determined the overall direction for recreation
services. The decision was made to combine both the Recreation and Library Divisions under the
Community Services Department. Similar to the Library Board of Trustees, this new Commission
serves to advise staff and Council on all matters related to comprehensive recreation programs,
services, user fees, and the soon-to-be re-opened San Marino Center operations. Director
Johnson, Recreation Manager Covarrubias, and Management Analyst Shigenaga will support this
Commission’s monthly meetings. The new Commissioners are:
  • Edward Yen, Chairperson
  • Cori Solan, Vice Chairperson
  • Roland Tam, Commissioner
  • Leslie Tsai, Commissioner
  • Stanley Wu, Commissioner

Barth Community Room in High Demand
In-person public meetings have reconvened for City Council, as well as for the 5 other advisory
bodies. Because the San Marino Center will be under construction soon, and physical distancing is
still recommended while pandemic conditions linger, public meetings are scheduled to be held in
the Barth Room instead of City Hall’s Council Chambers, which is slightly smaller. All meetings are
also offered virtually. It is recommended that you check the location of any public meeting before
attending, as locations are subject to change.

San Marino Public Library Foundation (SMPLF) Update
  Literary Libations - The Foundation is working toward the upcoming Literary Libations
  event at the Library. Alexander's Prime Meats and Catering is returning as the caterer and
  coordinating various tastings. The menu includes wagyu sliders, carnitas tostadas, sashimi, a
  charcuterie table, and a caviar tasting station. There will be tastings of beer, champagne,
  wine, and whiskey as guests roam the Library to experience the literary vignettes designed
  by Board Members.

  The silent auction includes a variety of options ranging from a cabin at Bass Lake to Danny
  Elfman tickets at the Hollywood Bowl to Dodger tickets. Board Members are busy
  procuring items and welcome any donations to the auction.

  The Foundation received strong sponsorship support and individual ticket sales are
  beginning. There is a deadline of September 30 to be included in the event program and
  other promotional elements. Sponsorships and tickets can be purchased at the Library’s

  Page 10 of 27
   Circulation Desk, online at sanmarinoplf.org, through a Board Member, or via mail. To
  date, there are over 30 sponsors committed to supporting the event.

  Foundation Board Members - One Board Member needed to step away from serving
  on the Board in July. The Board invited Zillah Tobiano to join in July and accepted. The
  Board currently consists of 17 board members.

Friends of Crowell Public Library
The Friends are planning activities for National Friends of Libraries Week, which occurs October
16-22. They will also be planning a One Book One City Event that will support DEI initiatives. In
addition to their programming activities, the Friends are researching establishing their own
website.

 Operational Staff Briefings
  Adult Programs
  Huntington Nurses Health Screening
  Huntington Hospital’s Nurses’ outreach continues at Crowell Public Library, with patrons
  being screened for hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes.

  Chinese Club of San Marino
  On July 14, the Chinese Club provided a hands-on lesson on Chinese knotting. This fine art
  has its roots in antiquity and is believed to have evolved from folk art. 13 participants had
  the opportunity to make bracelets using Chinese knotting techniques. On August 11, the
  Chinese Club provided a hands-on lesson on Dough Figurines. 3 participants had the
  opportunity to make their own welcome sign out of the dough.

  Toastmasters Talk of the Town
  San Marino’s Toastmasters group had 12 people at their two meetings in July and 5 people
  coming to their meetings in August. Participants were offered the opportunity to hone their
  presentation and speaking skills in a supportive and convenient setting.

  Joyful Living, Happy Life
  On July 10, the Library was pleased to once again partner with the United Charity
  Foundation. Attendees discussed how to go from ordinary to extraordinary and be the best
  version of themselves. This program was offered in Mandarin.

  Youth Programs
  Encanto Sing-Along
  On July 6, families were treated to a sing-along musical extravaganza of the film, Encanto,
  complete with audience participation prop goody bags. Between renditions of “We Don’t
  Talk About Bruno,” kids scattered flower petals, shook their shaky eggs, and ducked from
  “falling rain” (Library staff with squirt bottles).

  Family Storytime Kick-Off
  On August 9, the Library’s weekly Storytime program evolved to a mixed-ages offering to
  be more inclusive to patrons, and also accommodate the current staffing levels in the Youth
  Services area. This program has been very popular, with attendance ranging from 34 – 59
  people per session so far. Be sure to ask regular attendee, Chairperson Domier, to model
  the “Hello, Friends” song with sign language!

  Outreach
  Youth Services Librarian Torres represented the Library at the San Marino Unified School
  District’s elementary schools and middle school “Back to School Nights.” With her prize
  wheel in tow, she met with many families, promoted library services and programs, and gave
  out free prize books.

  Passports
  Passport Services continue to be in high demand. In the month of July, 276 passports were
  processed, which resulted in $11,000 in revenue. In the month of August, 347 passports
  were processed, which resulted in $13,885 in revenue.

   Crain Art Gallery
  The Gallery received a donation of $250 from artist Dilmit Singh for sales during her “Light
  and Literature” exhibit, which ended on July 22.

  An exhibit of brush paintings by Wang Xiali was on display from July 30 – September 8,
  with over 80 people attending a reception for her on July 30.

  The current exhibit displays landscape paintings by the Plein Aires, a group of 20 artists

SUBJECT:  FY 2021-22 BUDGET & DONATIONS MONITORS

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Management Analyst provides a quarterly
update of the Library’s financial condition. This report provides a macro view of the Library’s
fiscal health; it also includes information on projects funded through the Capital Improvement
Plan (CIP).

DISCUSSION

Attachments 1 and 2 are the year-end financial reports for FY 2021-22. Below are some high-
level comments for quarter 4 (Q4) and the year-end in general.

General Fund:
  • Revenue:
  o Passport fees continued to be the largest source of General Fund revenue
  o In Q4, the Library was able to offer room rentals, as a result of the relaxation of
  COVID-19 protocols, bringing in some revenue
  o Several line items did not bring in expected revenue, but higher than expected
  passport revenue more than offset those shortfalls
  • Expense:
  o Contract Services budget was not all spent
   Adult and Children’s Services budgets were padded with some “backfill”
  during the budget development process since staff expected fewer
  donations than usual. Some of this money was spent, but expenses are
  shown in the line item that they most appropriately are categorized in
   Chinese cataloging did not occur resulting in unspent money in the
  Processing budget
  o Planned purchases of non-capitalized equipment did not occur; some items were
  not needed and others have been budgeted for in current fiscal year

  Page 15 of 27
   o Overall spending on Library materials (books, e-resources, etc.) was low (spent
  about 73% of budget) due to vacancies in positions that have the responsibility to
  develop the collection; spending did pick up in Q4

Donations Fund:
  • Revenue:
  o Chinese Club of San Marino donated $1,000 for Adult Chinese Language Materials
  in Q4
  • Expense:
  o Minimal spending of donation monies in Q4 due to direction to spend General
  Fund monies first
  • $6,966 of unspent revenue will hit the Reserve Fund Balance (table in upper right corner
  of Attachment 2) when the Finance Department updates the balances in October /
  November 2022

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board receive and file the FY 2021-22 Budget and Donations Monitors.

SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF LIBRARY CLOSURE CALENDAR FOR 2023

BACKGROUND

Each year, staff present a closure calendar for the Crowell Public Library to the Board of Trustees,
and ultimately seek City Council’s approval. Council approval is needed to close on any days that
are not City approved holidays.

DISCUSSION

Staff are requesting the below closures for the Crowell Public Library in 2023:
  • Martin Luther King, Jr. Day (January 16): historically, the Library has been closed to the
  public in order to allow staff to participate in an all-day training. The goal is to offer a
  CPR/First Aid/AED training (8 hours).
  • Easter Sunday (April 9): historically, the Library has been closed to the public, as
  circulation and gate count has been lower than an average Sunday.
  • Thanksgiving Eve (November 22): staff are proposing an early closure (5 PM) due to
  historically low number of patrons in the building on this day.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board approve of the Library closure calendar for 2023 and request
City Council’s approval.

SUBJECT:  FINAL REPORT ON  ACCOMPLISHMENTS  FROM  2016-21
  STRATEGIC PLAN

BACKGROUND

Adopted in July 2016, the Library’s 5-year Strategic Plan was launched with the intent to guide
the Library’s successful operations from 2016-2021. It was a collaborative effort between the
Library Board of Trustees, City Administration, and Library Staff. The Strategic Plan consists of 5
overarching goals: 1) provide collection, programs, and services consistent with the
needs/expectations of the community; 2) develop and deliver outstanding services; 3) implement
efficient operations and secure financial support; 4) raise library awareness and visibility; and 5)
analyze ways to continually improve, excel, and maintain top ranking.

The purpose of this report is to provide a status update on each goal and objective, or explain if
an item has been identified as ongoing and best business practice for a community library.

DISCUSSION

Crowell Public Library’s Strategic Plan touches on all aspects of library service, including:
programming, collection development, outreach, and customer service. It is the current staffs’
professional opinion that an overwhelming majority of the goals are not representative of
standalone, measurable outcomes. Rather, they are more representative of industry best practice.
When these best practices are implemented and aligned consistently with community interests,
the Library is able to best meet the needs of its customers.

For example, the first objective of Goal One is to “Enhance collections through coordinated
collection development which is diverse and relevant…” This is an ongoing practice because
relevance lies in the nexus of community interest and shifts in technology or current events.
While there are moments when the shift is sudden and the need to respond to a single
occurrence is immediate, it is more often the case that the needle for relevance moves slowly
over time.

  Page 21 of 27
 While the pandemic did impact the Library’s ability to put some of these best practices into play,
staff are pleased to report that as the restrictions regarding social distancing have relaxed, staff
have prioritized operationalizing each of these strategic goals. See Attachment 1 for a status
update and deliverables identified by staff for each of the goals and objectives.

In conclusion, the goals outlined in the 2016-21 Strategic Plan road map established a foundation
for library operations moving forward. It is also the expectation of Library Administration that
staff continue the process of evaluation and implementation established. Working to implement
and operationalize these goals has been a valuable exercise for long standing and new staff. Staff
will continue to make sure the collection, services, and programs provided are meeting the needs
of all community members.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board receive and file the final report on accomplishments from 2016-
21 Strategic Plan.

  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

Barth Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared an update on his goals for the Board, reminded all of the Board’s role
and function, and thanked various parties including the Board and City staff.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Vice Chairperson Sadun shared an update about Sierra Madre Public Library and its lawn signs
displayed in front of various homes, money received for a remodel, and their Friends of the Library.
She also shared about her recent trip to a library in San Diego and spoke about the various programs
and services offered that meet the needs of the community.

Trustee Chien, Trustee Derry, Trustee Osegueda, Alternate Wahl, and Alternate Wu did not have
anything to report at this time.
